newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arnotts says to rationalise in Asia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arnotts says to rationalise in Asia.

text.p: Bakery group Arnotts Ltd said on Thursday it would rationalise its business in Asia to focus on one or two markets, rather than four as at present.
"I think our shot has been spread a little widely and we will be more focused and hopefully more successful," managing director Chris Roberts told the annual general meeting.
"We will probably focus in one or two markets there and make a success of them and then expand once again."
Responding to a shareholder's question, he said the company's challenge was to turn the inroads it had made in Asian markets into profitable trading.
Roberts said Arnotts, which is about 70 percent owned by Campbell Soup Co, would aim to improve its technical and human resources in Asia.
"At the moment we are selling, in serious terms, in four countries in Asia and not one of those is profitable," he said.
"The problem that we have is that as far forward as we look it's going to be unprofitable for us to be there."
Asked later by reporters which markets the company might exit, he said Arnotts was still considering its position.
However, he stressed the company wanted to make a success of Asia.
Arnotts has a 50 per cent share in Indonesian biscuit and snack company PT Helios Arnotts Indonesia, and exports its products to Taiwan, Hong Kong, South Korea, Japan and Singapore.
Arnotts increased net profit by 7.7 percent to A$60.9 million in the 13 months to July 28 this year.
Arnotts shares were down five cents at A$8.40 at 1.50 p.m. (0250 GMT) on Thursday.
